p: Trafford Park is packed with offices, warehouses and business units, so it's no surprise this is a popular spot for work events. Racing gets people mixing in a way that a pub night or a meeting-room team-building session never quite manages.

For the best results, think about the format. Dividing colleagues into mixed teams can make it less about the naturally competitive few and more about everyone pulling together. Ask about corporate and group options when you book, and get numbers confirmed early.

Remember that not everyone will be confident behind the wheel. A quick word to reassure nervous colleagues goes a long way. They'll get a proper briefing, and the lap timing means most people end up racing against themselves rather than worrying about others.

A final practical point: send round a reminder about flat, closed shoes and comfortable clothing the day before. Work groups often come straight from the office, and smart shoes or heels aren't ideal for a kart, so a quick heads-up saves a last-minute scramble.

Getting there is easier than it used to be. The Metrolink's Trafford Park line opened in 2020, linking the area to Manchester city centre, and the Trafford Centre is right on the line for anyone who wants to combine a race with a bit of shopping or a meal. Old Trafford cricket ground is also close by, so it's worth checking for big match days, when the area gets busy.
